Argument Default Meaning URL required fsspec URL to mount, such as s3://bucket/prefix or file:///data. MOUNTPOINT required Existing directory to mount on. -o KEY=VALUE, --option none Storage option passed to the backend as a string. Repeat for more options. --threads N 4 Number of requests served at once. -h, --help off Show help and exit. An option without = or with an empty key is rejected before mounting. t: How one mount reaches Rust and Python backends
x: How one mount reaches Rust and Python backends fsspec-fuse is one program that mounts URLs served by Rust backends, such as file:// and s3:// from fsspec-rs, and URLs served only by Python packages, such as gcsfs. This page explains how that works, what it costs, and why mounts start out read-only. One registry per process fsspec-rs ships a shared library, libfsspec, that holds the filesystem registry for the whole process. Rust extensions such as fsspec-db and fsspec-kafka register their protocols there, and fsspec-fuse looks URLs up there. When no native backend claims a protocol, the registry’s fallback hands the URL to Python fsspec, which finds the installed backend by protocol name. The alternative would be a mount program per backend, or one that only knows the backends it was compiled with. fsspec.fuse.run, the mount helper inside fsspec, takes the opposite route: it is pure Python, so it reaches every Python backend, but every request runs Python code. fsspec-fuse keeps native requests out of the interpreter and uses Python only for the backends that exist only there. t: How one mount reaches Rust and Python backends
s: The cost of a Python backend
x: A request against a Python backend has to take the GIL. Each FUSE request runs on one of the mount’s threads, which waits for the GIL, calls the backend, and replies. The Python code in those calls runs one request at a time, though backends that release the GIL while waiting on the network, as most do, still overlap their waits. Native backends do not touch the interpreter, so their requests run fully in parallel. The GIL also explains how a process can mount a Python backend and read from it at the same time. Python releases the GIL during blocking file calls such as os.listdir and open, so a mount thread can take it while the reading thread waits. Native code that reads the mount while holding the GIL would block the thread that serves it. Running the mount in its own process, as the fsspec-fuse command does, avoids that case.

t: How one mount reaches Rust and Python backends
x: A local filesystem lets a program write a few bytes into the middle of a file. Object stores do not: S3 replaces a whole object on every write. A writable mount over S3 has to collect a file’s writes and upload the complete object when the file closes, and it has to report a failed upload on close rather than on the write that caused it. Renames become a copy followed by a delete. mountpoint-s3, AWS’s S3 mount, handles this by allowing only sequential writes to new files. Another approach buffers each open file, which costs memory or temporary disk but allows random writes. fsspec-fuse started read-only so that behavior is the same on every backend while a write design is chosen.

t: How one mount reaches Rust and Python backends
x: A FUSE filesystem tells the kernel how long it may cache what it learns. fsspec-fuse lets the kernel cache attributes and lookups for one second and lists a directory once per open. A file changed by another writer appears within about a second, and nothing coordinates between separate mounts of the same bucket. Longer caching would cut requests to remote backends at the cost of staler listings.

Install FUSE On Debian or Ubuntu, install FUSE 3: sudo apt-get install fuse3 On macOS, install macFUSE and approve its system extension when macOS asks: brew install --cask macfuse Mount an S3 bucket from the command line Pass the URL, the mount point, and the backend’s storage options with -o: fsspec-fuse s3://warehouse/reports /mnt/reports \ -o region=us-east-1 -o key=ACCESS_KEY -o secret=SECRET_KEY For an S3-compatible service such as MinIO, add its endpoint: fsspec-fuse s3://warehouse/reports /mnt/reports \ -o endpoint_url=http://localhost:9000 -o region=us-east-1 \ -o key=minioadmin -o secret=minioadmin Use -o anon=true for a public bucket. On AWS, leave out key and secret to use the standard credential chain. The command keeps running while the bucket is mounted; press Ctrl-C to unmount. On AWS, leave out key and secret to use the standard credential chain. The command keeps running while the bucket is mounted; press Ctrl-C to unmount. The S3 options are listed under “S3Fs” in the fsspec-rs reference.

Call mount with storage options as keyword arguments, and use it as a context manager so the filesystem unmounts when the block ends: import os from fsspec_fuse import mount with mount("s3://warehouse/reports", "/mnt/reports", region="us-east-1", anon=True): print(os.listdir("/mnt/reports")) To keep the mount past one block, hold the returned object and call unmount() when done.

s: Mount a backend that only exists in Python
x: Install the backend’s package in the same environment, then mount its URL. fsspec-fuse finds Python fsspec backends by protocol, so a public Google Cloud Storage bucket mounts with gcsfs: python -m pip install gcsfs fsspec-fuse gcs://my-public-bucket/data /mnt/data -o token=anon Storage options reach the Python backend as strings.

Raise --threads (or threads= in Python) when many processes read the mount at once or the backend has high latency: fsspec-fuse s3://warehouse/reports /mnt/reports -o anon=true --threads 16 The default is 4.

If the mounting process was killed before it could unmount, the mount point reports “Transport endpoint is not connected”. Unmount it by hand: fusermount3 -u /mnt/reports # Linux umount /mnt/reports # macOS

Each path gets an inode number the first time it is looked up. Numbers are not reused, so a mount that visits many paths keeps a growing table for its lifetime.

fsspec-fuse Mount fsspec filesystems with FUSE Build Status codecov License PyPI Overview fsspec-fuse mounts an fsspec URL as a read-only local directory, so any program can list and read it with ordinary file operations. fsspec-fuse s3://my-bucket/reports /mnt/reports -o region=us-east-1 ls /mnt/reports URLs resolve through the filesystem registry that fsspec-rs shares between extensions. Native backends (file://, s3://, and protocols registered by packages such as fsspec-db and fsspec-kafka) run in Rust. Any other protocol falls back to the Python fsspec implementation installed for it, such as gcsfs or adlfs. From Python, mount returns a handle that unmounts on unmount() or when its with block ends: import os from fsspec_fuse import mount with mount("s3://my-bucket/reports", "/mnt/reports", region="us-east-1"): print(os.listdir("/mnt/reports")) Storage options pass to the backend as strings. threads sets how many requests the mount serves at once (default 4).
